microtheory.name: cell_biology
microtheory.definition: The cell as fundamental unit of life. Organelles, membrane, cytoskeleton, signaling, division, communication. Cell theory (Schleiden + Schwann + Virchow). Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept as basic unit + Mt as functional cell-analogue.

concepts.name: cell_theory
concepts.definition: Schleiden + Schwann 1839, Virchow 1855. All life made of cells; cells are basic units; cells come from cells. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional principle.

concepts.name: prokaryote
concepts.definition: No nucleus. Bacteria + archaea. Small, no membrane organelles. Substrate analogue: substrate's atomic Mt without internal hierarchy.

concepts.name: eukaryote
concepts.definition: Nucleus + membrane organelles. All multicellular life + many single-celled. Substrate analogue: substrate's hierarchical Mt.

concepts.name: cell_membrane
concepts.definition: Phospholipid bilayer. Selectively permeable. Boundary between inside + outside. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt boundary.

concepts.name: selective_permeability
concepts.definition: Membrane lets some things through, blocks others. Channels, transporters. Substrate analogue: substrate's edge-type filtering.

concepts.name: ion_channel
concepts.definition: Membrane protein selectively passing ions. Voltage-gated, ligand-gated. Foundation of neural signaling. Substrate analogue: substrate's gated communication.

concepts.name: membrane_potential_cell
concepts.definition: Voltage across membrane. ~-70mV in neurons. Action potential = brief flip. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ state.

concepts.name: nucleus
concepts.definition: Eukaryotic organelle housing DNA. Nuclear envelope. Nucleolus inside. Substrate analogue: substrate's foundational Mt store.

concepts.name: mitochondrion
concepts.definition: Energy-producing organelle. ATP synthesis via oxidative phosphorylation. Endosymbiont origin. Substrate analogue: substrate's energy-providing subsystem.

concepts.name: endoplasmic_reticulum
concepts.definition: Rough (with ribosomes, protein synthesis) + smooth (lipid synthesis, detox). Substrate analogue: substrate's processing pipeline.

concepts.name: golgi_apparatus
concepts.definition: Processes + packages proteins for export. Substrate analogue: substrate's output preparation.

concepts.name: lysosome
concepts.definition: Acidic compartment digesting waste + recycled components. Substrate analogue: substrate's pruning mechanism.

concepts.name: cytoskeleton
concepts.definition: Internal scaffold. Microtubules, actin filaments, intermediate filaments. Shape + transport + division. Substrate analogue: substrate's structural skeleton.

concepts.name: chloroplast
concepts.definition: Plant organelle performing photosynthesis. Endosymbiont origin like mitochondria. Substrate analogue: substrate's energy-capture from environment.

concepts.name: cell_signaling
concepts.definition: How cells communicate. Endocrine, paracrine, juxtacrine, autocrine. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-Mt signaling.

concepts.name: receptor
concepts.definition: Protein binding signal + transducing it. GPCRs, RTKs, ion channels. Substrate analogue: substrate's input concept.

concepts.name: ligand
concepts.definition: Molecule binding receptor. Hormones, neurotransmitters, growth factors. Substrate analogue: substrate's signal value.

concepts.name: signaling_cascade
concepts.definition: Chain of intracellular events from receptor to response. Amplification + integration. Substrate analogue: substrate's chained activation.

concepts.name: second_messenger
concepts.definition: Intracellular signal molecule. cAMP, IP3, Ca2+. Substrate analogue: substrate's relay signal.

concepts.name: cell_cycle
concepts.definition: G1 → S → G2 → M. Checkpoints prevent damage propagation. Substrate analogue: substrate's update cycle with checkpoints.

concepts.name: mitosis
concepts.definition: Cell division producing two identical diploid cells. Substrate analogue: substrate's state-copy.

concepts.name: meiosis
concepts.definition: Reduction division for gametes. Crossing over creates variation. Substrate analogue: substrate's variation-producing reproduction.

concepts.name: apoptosis
concepts.definition: Programmed cell death. Controlled, anti-inflammatory. Essential for development + homeostasis. Substrate analogue: substrate's controlled Mt removal.

concepts.name: cancer
concepts.definition: Uncontrolled cell proliferation from accumulated mutations. Substrate analogue: substrate's unchecked runaway expansion.

concepts.name: stem_cell
concepts.definition: Self-renewing + differentiation-capable cell. Embryonic + adult. Substrate analogue: substrate's generative Concept node.

concepts.name: cell_differentiation
concepts.definition: Cell becoming specialized type via gene expression program. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt specialization.

concepts.name: potency
concepts.definition: Range of cell types a stem cell can become. Toti-, pluri-, multi-, unipotent. Substrate analogue: substrate's generative range.

concepts.name: endosymbiosis
concepts.definition: Margulis 1967. Eukaryotic organelles (mito, chloro) from engulfed bacteria. Major evolutionary transition. Substrate analogue: substrate's integration of external modules.

concepts.name: multicellularity
concepts.definition: Major transition. Cells differentiate + cooperate. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-Mt cooperation.

concepts.name: homeostasis_cellular
concepts.definition: Cell's internal regulation. pH, osmotic balance, energy state. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-level stability.

rules.name: membrane_boundary_defines_self_nonself
rules.head: the substrate maintains a boundary between internal + external
rules.body: selective permeability lets it choose what enters + exits. Substrate's Mt boundary as self/non-self distinction.

rules.name: signaling_cascade_amplifies_and_integrates
rules.head: the substrate receives multiple signals
rules.body: intracellular cascades amplify + integrate them before output. Substrate's chained Mt activation.

rules.name: checkpoints_prevent_error_propagation
rules.head: the substrate divides or duplicates
rules.body: checkpoints verify integrity before proceeding. Damage detection halts cycle. Substrate's verification gates.

rules.name: apoptosis_eliminates_compromised_cells
rules.head: the substrate has a damaged or unwanted component
rules.body: programmed removal eliminates it cleanly. Substrate's controlled Mt removal.

rules.name: endosymbiosis_drives_complexity_jumps
rules.head: the substrate integrates an externally-developed module
rules.body: the integration creates new capability levels. Endosymbiosis → eukaryotes. Substrate's modular-integration major transitions.
